S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.

subtypes.Negative Self-Beliefs: Distorted beliefs such as 'I am fundamentally bad,' 'I am damaged,' or 'I am worthless'.
subtypes.Negative Beliefs about Others: Distorted beliefs such as 'No one can be trusted' or 'Others are dangerous'.
subtypes.Negative Worldview: Extreme beliefs such as 'The world is completely dangerous' or 'Life is meaningless'.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.

subtypes.Self-Blame: Blaming oneself for the occurrence of the trauma or for not preventing it.
subtypes.Blaming Others: Distorting the situation to blame specific others for the occurrence or damage of the trauma.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.

subtypes.Scanning for Danger: Always scanning the surroundings and being alert to find potential threats or risks.
subtypes.Safety Checking: Repetitively confirming safety, such as checking exit locations or observing people around.
subtypes.Sustained Alertness: Unable to relax tension even in safe environments and maintaining a constant state of alertness.

info.persona: Georgina Howe is a socially savvy, curiosity‑driven quality‑control veteran who blends hands‑on problem‑solving with a relaxed, slightly scattered approach to life, constantly juggling community projects, health quirks, and a love of garden‑fresh meals.
info.professional_persona: Georgina Howe, a veteran quality control specialist in manufacturing, leverages their expertise in equipment calibration, statistical process control, and regulatory compliance to mentor new staff, while their relaxed yet curious mindset lets them adapt inspection protocols on the fly and champion a culture of safety and continuous improvement.
info.cultural_background: Georgina was raised in Erie, Pennsylvania, within a predominantly white, working‑class community rooted in the region’s manufacturing heritage. Her family background includes Irish and German ancestry, shaping values of hard work, reliability, and community support. Growing up near the Great Lakes, she internalized a pragmatic Midwestern ethos—practicality, friendliness, and a strong sense of local pride. Participation in church and neighborhood events fostered a cooperative spirit, while the industrial backdrop encouraged an appreciation for technical skills and safety. These cultural influences inform her respectful, community‑oriented outlook and her commitment to both personal and collective well‑being.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Georgina enjoys staying active in her community and loves group activities that blend social interaction with creativity. She participates in a community theater group, a local book club, and a line‑dancing class at the senior center. Gardening and cooking are favorite pastimes, especially when she can share meals with friends and neighbors. She volunteers at the regional food bank, hikes along Presque Isle State Park trails, and pursues crafts like knitting and quilting. Her curiosity also leads her to explore Erie’s industrial history, often visiting museums and documenting stories of local factories.
info.sports_persona: Georgina Howe stays active by line‑dancing at the senior center, hiking the coastal trails of Presque Isle State Park, and cheering on the Erie SeaWolves minor‑league baseball team; they blend low‑impact exercise with the camaraderie of group activities.
info.arts_persona: Georgina Howe thrives in community theater, where they perform in productions ranging from Shakespeare to modern comedies, leads a book club that debates works by Toni Morrison and Margaret Atwood, and knits intricate quilts inspired by folk artist Grandma Moses, making the arts a central thread of their social life.
info.travel_persona: Georgina Howe prefers weekend road trips to industrial heritage sites such as the Pennsylvania Railroad Museum in Strasburg and the historic mills of Meadville, and they dream of a summer getaway to Cape Cod’s lighthouse trails, balancing curiosity about manufacturing history with a love for coastal scenery.
info.culinary_persona: Georgina Howe relishes cooking farm‑to‑table meals, often preparing roasted beet salad with goat cheese, hearty chicken pot pie, and herb‑infused focaccia; they use fresh herbs from their garden and share generous portions with neighbors after community theater rehearsals.

info.persona: Peter Deloach blends a compassionate storyteller's heart with a relaxed, slightly disorganized painter's mind, often losing his favorite brush in the garden but never missing an opportunity to share a local legend over a cup of tea.
info.professional_persona: Peter Deloach, a retired senior-center volunteer coordinator, merges his woodworking, gardening, and first-aid expertise with a storyteller's flair to mentor younger residents, organize community art shows, and preserve local history through oral narratives.
info.cultural_background: Peter grew up in the heart of rural Indiana, steeped in Midwestern values of community, modesty, and self‑reliance. His family’s roots trace back to early European immigrants—primarily German and Irish—who settled in Jasper County to farm the land. The local culture emphasized church involvement, seasonal festivals, high school sports, and strong neighborhood ties. This background fostered Peter’s deep appreciation for cooperative endeavors, respect for tradition, and a love of practical arts. His upbringing in a small‑town setting shaped his easygoing, compassionate demeanor and his desire to contribute to the well‑being of his community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Peter’s leisure pursuits reflect his imaginative and compassionate nature. He spends many afternoons painting landscapes and still‑life subjects in watercolor, exploring new techniques and color palettes. He enjoys reading historical non‑fiction and biographies, which feed his intellectual curiosity. Gardening, especially tending to tomatoes, roses, and native wildflowers, offers him both creativity and a quiet space for reflection. He plays the harmonica for personal enjoyment and occasionally at local gatherings. Peter also loves walking the nearby nature trails, researching his family’s genealogy, and volunteering as a storyteller at the senior center, where he shares anecdotes and local legends.
info.sports_persona: Peter Deloach stays active by strolling the nearby nature trails with the Trailblazers Walking Club, participates in the senior center's Thursday bowling league, enjoys seasonal bird-watching hikes in spring, and remains an avid fan of the Chicago Cubs and the New York Yankees, cheering them on from his porch while never missing the weekly senior-friendly yoga class at the community gym.
info.arts_persona: Peter Deloach expresses his artistic soul through delicate watercolors inspired by Claude Monet and Winslow Homer, plays the harmonica to the tunes of Bob Dylan and Pete Seeger at local gatherings, reads biographies of John James Audubon and Mary Cassatt for creative inspiration, and volunteers as a storyteller at the senior center, weaving local legends into compelling performances.
info.travel_persona: Peter Deloach favors relaxed, senior-discount road trips that combine historical exploration with natural scenery, having visited Colonial Williamsburg, Gettysburg Battlefield, and the Blue Ridge Mountains, while dreaming of a leisurely pilgrimage to the Scottish Highlands and a cultural tour of the Roman ruins in Italy, always planning itineraries around comfortable lodging and ample time for watercolor sketching.
info.culinary_persona: Peter Deloach enjoys cooking simple, garden-fresh meals such as heirloom tomato basil soup, rosemary-infused roasted carrots, and rosehip jam for toast, demonstrates moderate culinary prowess by experimenting with fresh herbs like thyme and sage, and occasionally treats himself to a classic pot roast with root vegetables, all while savoring the occasional slice of homemade apple pie.

info.persona: Katherine Martinez fuses analytical precision with sociable energy, turning every code review, trail hike, and dinner party into a collaborative, curiosity‑driven experience, even if occasional procrastination on tax filing slips through the cracks.
info.professional_persona: Katherine Martinez, a computer systems analyst with three years of experience, blends her curiosity for emerging technologies with a methodical, organized approach to translate business requirements into scalable cloud architectures, leveraging Python, Java, and AWS while energizing cross-functional teams with her sociable, talkative facilitation style.
info.cultural_background: Katherine grew up in a middle-class, predominantly Anglo-American household in the Hudson River Valley, where community events, local history, and a strong work ethic are valued. The region’s mix of rural charm and proximity to New York City exposed her to both traditional Upstate New York customs—farmers markets, county fairs, and a love for the outdoors—and a diverse, multicultural environment that fostered her inclusive outlook. While identifying as white, her family’s Spanish surname reflects a blended heritage, and she often celebrates this by participating in cultural festivals and speaking Spanish with extended relatives, adding a bilingual dimension to her social interactions.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Katherine channels her curiosity and sociable nature into a mix of active, creative, and community-focused pursuits. She explores the Hudson Valley's trails on weekend hikes, practices yoga for balance, and enjoys photographing landscapes and street scenes. Katherine volunteers as a coding mentor for middle-school girls, runs a local women-in-tech meetup, and participates in Toastmasters to sharpen her public speaking. She also loves hosting dinner parties where she experiments with new recipes, plays board games with friends, and unwinds with sci-fi novels and strategy video games.
info.sports_persona: Katherine Martinez, an avid hiker of the Hudson Valley trails, seasonally plays recreational soccer with a local women's league, follows the New York Knicks and New York Rangers, and commits to a weekly yoga class to maintain flexibility and stress resilience.
info.arts_persona: Katherine Martinez, an enthusiastic photographer inspired by Ansel Adams, captures both sweeping Hudson Valley vistas and vibrant street scenes, curates a Spotify playlist featuring synth‑wave artist Kavinsky and indie folk band Fleet Foxes, and regularly attends off‑Broadway productions starring Lin‑Manuel Miranda and contemporary art openings at the Hudson Valley Center for Contemporary Art.
info.travel_persona: Katherine Martinez, who prefers a blend of adventure and cultural immersion, meticulously plans weekend getaways to nearby Finger Lakes wineries and long‑distance treks in the Appalachian Trail, while dreaming of a summer immersion in Reykjavik’s geothermal pools and a spring cherry‑blossom tour of Kyoto, balancing travel costs with her savings goals.
info.culinary_persona: Katherine Martinez, a self‑taught home chef who delights in experimenting with dishes like spicy Sichuan mapo tofu, Mediterranean grilled octopus, and homemade sourdough, often incorporates seasonal ingredients such as heirloom tomatoes, fresh basil, and locally sourced mushrooms, and pairs her meals with craft IPA selections from New York breweries.
